intro: The passive (The bridge was built in 1950) puts the focus on what receives the action rather than who does it. It is very common in English, in the news, science, work and instructions.
objectifs: Form the passive in the present simple (is / are + participle) and past simple (was / were + participle), in all forms.
Know when to choose the passive: the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant, or we want to focus on the object.
Use by to name the doer only when it is useful.
Replace general subjects (people, they, someone) with a passive in more formal English.

texte: We make the passive with be in the right tense and the past participle of the main verb. Be carries the tense: is / are in the present, was / were in the past. The participle never changes.

To change an active sentence into a passive one, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject: “Someone stole my bike” → “My bike was stolen”. Only verbs with an object (transitive verbs) can be passive: we can't say “It was happened”.

lignes: Yes, it is. / No, it isn't.
Yes, it was. / No, they weren't.

texte: We choose the passive when the doer is unknown (My car was stolen), obvious (He was arrested — by the police, of course) or unimportant (The rooms are cleaned every day).
We also use it to keep the same subject from one sentence to the next, or to focus on the result: “The Pont de Normandie is one of the longest bridges in France. It was opened in 1995.”

The passive is typical of impersonal writing: reports, news articles, science, rules. In speech, we often use you, they or people instead: “They speak French in Quebec” = “French is spoken in Quebec”.
exemples: My phone was stolen on the bus.
Thousands of new cars are sold every day.
The suspect was arrested last night.
Coffee is grown in the west of Cameroon.
Focus on the coffee, not the farmers.

texte: When the doer is important or new information, we name it with by: “Guernica was painted by Picasso.” The important information then comes at the end of the sentence, where English naturally puts new information.
If the doer is vague (someone, people, they) or obvious, don't use by: “My wallet was stolen by someone” sounds strange. Use with for an instrument: “The door was opened with a key.”
exemples: Things Fall Apart was written by Chinua Achebe.
The writer is the key information.
The new hospital was opened by the president.
By + the person who did it.
The cake was cut with a sharp knife.

texte: Everyday English often uses a general subject (people, they, you, someone); more formal English prefers the passive. Both are correct, but the register is different.
With verbs like give, send, offer, tell and show, the person who receives can become the subject: “They gave me a present” → “I was given a present.” “Someone told me that…” → “I was told that…”

lignes: They built the castle in the 16th century.
The castle was built in the 16th century.

texte: The same idea works in every tense: be changes, the participle stays. Present continuous: “The road is being repaired.” Present perfect: “The tickets have been sold.”
These forms, the passive with modals (must be done) and the passive with reporting verbs (He is said to be…) are studied at B2 (lessons 151 and 152).
exemples: Sorry, the lift is being repaired.
All the tickets have been sold.

formule: is / are + participle (present) · was / were + participle (past) · + by + doer if useful
prononciation: is and was are weak in the passive: “It's made in Ghana” /ɪts ˈmeɪd/, “It was built” /ɪt wəz ˈbɪlt/.
were is weak /wə/: “They were sold” /ðeɪ wə ˈsəʊld/.
-ed in regular participles: /t/ after a voiceless sound (cooked /kʊkt/), /d/ after a voiced sound (cleaned /kliːnd/), /ɪd/ after t or d (painted /ˈpeɪntɪd/, decided).
The stress falls on the participle, which carries the meaning: “The car was STOLEN.” If by follows, the doer is stressed too: “painted by PICASSO”.
erreurs: After be, use the past participle (built), not the base verb.
A language doesn't speak: it is spoken → passive.
Happen has no object: no passive.
My bag was stolen by someone.
By + someone / people adds nothing: leave it out.
No preposition at the end of “Where were you born?”.
Use the past simple for birth: was / were born.

dialogue.contexte: A guided tour in Brussels. The guide, Marc, presents the Atomium to a group of tourists, including Fatima from Casablanca.
lignes: This is the Atomium. It was built for the 1958 World's Fair.
Question with by at the end.
It was designed by an engineer, André Waterkeyn.
Yes. Exhibitions are organised inside, and the top sphere is used as a restaurant.
Were the spheres always this shiny?
No, they weren't. The building was renovated in the 2000s and the old panels were replaced.
Short answer, then two past passives.

mots: to make a building, bridge, etc. (built, built)
The tower was designed by an engineer.
to plan how something will look and work
to take something that isn't yours (stole, stolen)
The telephone was invented in the 19th century.
to create something new for the first time
Is breakfast included in the price?
to contain as part of the whole
Cocoa is grown in Côte d'Ivoire.
to plant and look after crops (grew, grown)
Two men were arrested last night.
when the police take someone because of a crime

exercices.consigne: Say if the sentence is active (A) or passive (P).
items: Rice is grown in many Asian countries.

exercices.consigne: Put the verb in the passive (present simple or past simple, depending on the meaning).
items: French ___ (speak) in Belgium, Canada and Cameroon.

exercices.consigne: Put the sentence in the passive. Add by only if it is useful.
items: Someone stole my car last night.
My car was stolen last night.
They deliver the post at ten every day.
The post is delivered at ten every day.
Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie wrote this novel.
This novel was written by Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie.
They don't accept credit cards in this shop.
Credit cards aren't accepted in this shop.

exercices.consigne: Each sentence has one mistake. Write it correctly.
items: Coffee grows in Cameroon by farmers.
The accident was happened at night.

exercices.consigne: Rewrite each sentence with a passive.
items: People speak French and English in Cameroon.
French and English are spoken in Cameroon.

exercices.consigne: In 4–5 sentences, present a monument, product or speciality from your country or city, using at least four passives (present and past).
items: The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace is in Yamoussoukro. It was built between 1985 and 1989, and it was designed by Pierre Fakhoury. It is visited by thousands of tourists every year. Masses are still held there on Sundays.

a_retenir: Passive = be in the right tense + past participle: is / are done (present), was / were done (past).
Use it when the doer is unknown, obvious or unimportant.
By + doer only when it is useful information; with + instrument.
General subjects (people, they, someone) → passive in more formal English.
No passive for verbs without an object (happen, arrive, die); birth = was / were born.
